points.description: States the core advantage: passing by reference avoids copying the argument (especially large data structures/objects) when calling a function, so it is more efficient in time/memory.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if it only says it is 'more efficient' or 'faster' or 'saves memory' without saying copies are avoided.

points.description: Ties the advantage to large data structures/objects (e.g., big arrays, structs, classes) as the case where avoiding the copy matters.

rubric.notes: Full marks: says by-reference passing avoids copying the argument (so saves time/memory), ideally mentioning large data structures. Part marks: vague efficiency claims with no mention of avoiding copies, or the copy idea without mention of large data. No marks: only saying the function can modify the original, or unrelated points, without the avoid-copying idea.
